newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh hopes to sign deals with foreign oil cos by Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh hopes to sign deals with foreign oil cos by Dec 16.

text.p: Bangladesh said on Thursday that it expected to sign production-sharing deals on oil and gas exploration with foreign companies by December 16.
"We expect billions of dollars in foreign investment in oil and gas exploration in the coming years after we finalise the deals," Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan told a news conference.
He said the bidding for 15 exploration blocks, including three in the Bay of Bengal, would close on July 15 but that some bids had already been opened.
"Hopefully, we will be able to sign deals by December 16 following negotiations with the bidders," he said.
The bidding process began at investors' meetings in London and Houston in March. Some 60 leading companies of the world participated.
"We have briefed them (companies) about the potentials of oil and gas in Bangladesh, and provided them all necessary data," Khan said.
"The response from the companies was encouraging and I hope a huge investment will be pouring into Bangladesh," he said.
Officials said foreign oil companies were particularly interested after British Cairn Energy Plc found large natural gas reserves in the Bay of Bengal.
The Sangu field, which the Cairn discovered last year, is estimated to have gas reserves of about one trillion cubic feet (TCF).
Khan said Cairn was investing $188 million in the two offsore blocks.
He said Bangladesh had already offered eight blocks to foreign companies including Unocal Corp, Occidental Corp and United Meridian and it might attract investment of more than $800 million.
"More and more companies are showing interest because of our clear-cut policies and incentives," he said."

The officials said Bangladesh offers duty free imports of machinery, allows repatriation of profit, and exemption of administering fee and corporate tax. Besides, there is a clear policy on gas pricing.
Khan said the foreign companies would bear production costs but they would be allowed to recover the cost under the production-sharing contract. Bangladesh will buy gas or oil from them, he said.
"There is a huge need for gas in the country. We can produce fertiliser, liquified petroleum gas, diesel and kerosene," he said.
He said Bangladesh had already signed gas purchase agreements with Cairn for 165 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) and Occidental for 100 mmcfd at an international price.
Khan said Bangladesh now had proven gas reserves of 10 trillion cubic feet.
"But there is a (suspicion) that the country has huge gas reserve still undiscovered," he said.

The officials said major oil companies like American companies Exxon Corp, Mobil Corp, Union Texas Petroleum Holding Inc, Unocal Corp, British Petroleum and some French and Italian companies will be among the bidders.
